title: GlyphBench: mini-session latency + cost scan
summary: Working notes for an internal microbenchmark (GlyphBench) that compares latency and $/query for short interactive sessions (2-6 turns). Includes ASCII charts and quick heuristics for when payload compression + tiny-batch strategies beat plain multiplexing.
body:
Objective:
Quickly quantify latency and cost tradeoffs for "mini" interactive sessions (median length ~40 tokens / turn, 2-6 turns) across three serving strategies: 1) multiplexed small-batch (default fastpath), 2) tiny-session batching (session-affinity + sustained slot), 3) compressed-payload + opportunistic window. Goal is actionable heuristics for Console "fast-fallthrough" recommendations and a short blurb for the pricing/latency playbook.

Test matrix (concise):
- Models: rwin-13B-fp16 (baseline), rwin-7B-int4 (quantized candidate)
- Hardware: H100 (dense), A10G (edge-like), vGPU-slab (multi-tenant)
- Client pattern: Poisson arrivals tuned to average 0.6 sessions/sec per worker, 30% concurrency variability
- Session profile: 2, 4, 6 turns; turn lengths 20, 40, 80 tokens sampled from real production traces
- Strategies: multiplex-smallbatch (window 5ms), tiny-session (reserve slot ~50ms prewarm), compress-json (gzip on prompt, decompress mid-model)

Raw observations (median of 10 runs):
- p50 / p95 / p99 latencies (ms) for 4-turn, 40-token median: 
  * H100 / rwin-13B-fp16 / multiplex: p50=62, p95=210, p99=410
  * H100 / rwin-13B-fp16 / tiny-session: p50=78, p95=135, p99=220
  * H100 / rwin-7B-int4 / compress-json: p50=55, p95=120, p99=250
- $/1k queries (amortized token compute + infra cost estimate): 
  * multiplex (13B fp16): $7.8
  * tiny-session (13B fp16): $9.1 (higher due to reserved slot time)
  * quant+compress (7B int4): $3.2

ASCII chart — p95 tradeoff by strategy (lower is better):
p95 latency (ms)
H100:   multiplex [=====........] 210
        tiny    [======..... ] 135
        quant+z [====....... ] 120
A10G:   multiplex [========... ] 280
        tiny    [=====...... ] 160
        quant+z [====....... ] 140

Interpretation notes:
- Multiplex wins for uninterrupted tail when session burstiness is low; p50 lowest but p99 suffers in microbursts (queueing).
- Tiny-session reduces tail by giving affinity/prewarm but raises cost per query because reserved cycles sit idle between turns. Works best when sessions have >=3 turns and predictable inter-turn spacing.
- Quantized + compression gives the best $/query in most short-session mixes we tried; latency slightly better than tiny-session on average but p99 can be worse on noisy hosts. Compression helps most when prompt size > 800 bytes (long system prompts); otherwise decompression overhead offsets gains.

Heuristic thresholds (quick rules):
- If median session turns <= 2 and >50% sessions < 300ms inter-turn gap => multiplex with small-window.
- If median session turns >= 3 and inter-turn gap > 150ms => tiny-session affinity worth enabling for enterprise customers with latency SLOs.
- If payload average prompt size > 1KB and model can run int4 accurately => enable compress+quant pipeline and route lower-tier workloads to it for cost savings.

Open questions / TODO:
- Need p99 breakdown into serialization vs model vs scheduling. Add tracing spans in next run (linked to JIRA-OBS-429).
- Run same matrix on vGPU-slab with heavier noisy neighbors (simulate 40% noisy tenant CPU/GPU).
- Validate quality delta between rwin-13B fp16 and rwin-7B int4 on our standardized prompt set (small evals).

Quick action items:
- Evan: add span-level traces + attach to this doc (due 2029-07-09).
- María: run compressed-payload runs with brotli and compare; capture CPU cost for decompression.
- Ilya: synthetic noisy-tenant runs on vGPU by 2029-07-11.

Notes to self: this is a working sketch — avoid publishing to docs until we have p99 span breakdown and quality evals. Keep in mind channel routing: offer quant+compress as "economy with soft-SLA" and tiny-session as "latency-priority with higher per-query price".

References and rough links: CONFLUENCE-8247 (design), GH PR 991 (console wiring), JIRA-OBS-429 (trace task).
